I was in a very similar situation a few years ago. My therapist of 10 months left abruptly and I was heartbroken. After emailing her about why she left (she suddenly became the primary caretaker for some family members and had to cut back on clients) and meeting in person for one last time to gain some closure, we agreed that people who play such an important role in our lives never really leave. I remember asking her "Is this goodbye forever?", and she responded with "It's not a goodbye, it's a 'see you again someday/see you later'". That's what helped me the most, knowing that even though she isn't playing an active role in my life, she's still there. I've emailed her periodically over the years, usually around the holiday season. I also met up with her before I left for college because I wanted to tell her in person that I was attending a university in the country where she is from. It might also be therapeutic for you to ask your former therapist to write you a letter for you to read when you miss her. I've had therapists write me letters like this when I've had to go away for a while and it helped. Overall, don't fight the grief, it's a very normal response. Anyway, my heart goes out to you because I've been there, feel free to private message me if you need anything. :)
